questions.question: 2,5 kg of flour and a 750 ml bottle, converted:
A garden 8 m by 5 m needs fencing and ground cover:
options: Perimeter 26 m of fencing, area 40 m² of ground — 2 × (8 + 5) and 8 × 5

questions.question: Tank: radius 0,7 m, height 1,5 m, pi as 3,142. Volume is:
options: 6,598 m³ — using the diameter by mistake

questions.question: That 2,309 m³ tank holds, in litres:
options: About 2 309 litres — one cubic metre is 1 000 litres

questions.question: 7 cm measured on a 1 : 50 000 map is really:
options: 3,5 km — 350 000 cm walked down the unit ladder

questions.question: A 420 km trip at an average 100 km/h takes:
options: 4 hours 20 minutes — the decimal read as minutes

questions.question: A distance chart between towns is read by:
options: Adding the row and column totals
Running one town's row to the other's column — the crossing cell holds the kilometres

questions.question: On a marathon elevation chart, the steepest climb is where the line is:
options: Steepest — rising fastest, not sitting highest

questions.question: A wall measuring 62 mm on a 1 : 100 plan is really:
options: 6,2 m — 6 200 mm, and the 2-to-8-metre room check confirms it

questions.question: Heights of windows and roofs are found on:
options: The elevations — the floor plan cannot show UP

questions.question: The safe way to match an elevation to the floor plan:
options: Trust left and right as drawn
Pick the drawing with the most detail
Count the doors and windows the plan puts on each compass face and match the pattern — left and right flip outside

questions.question: A 10 m by 6 m stage modelled at 1 : 50 measures 20 cm by 12 cm, and its top area is:
options: One fiftieth of the real area
One two-thousand-five-hundredth — areas shrink by the scale factor SQUARED

questions.question: The probability of rolling a six, in three dialects:
Two coins: the probability of two heads is:
options: 1/4 — list all four outcomes first: HH, HT, TH, TT
1/3 — three outcomes: two heads, two tails, mixed

questions.question: 120 learners; 42 girls and 30 boys walk. P(a randomly chosen learner walks):
A 30% chance of rain means the chance of NO rain is:
A 15 m by 9 m hall, with each table needing 9 m², seats at 8 guests per table:
The fairy lights along the hall's edge need:
options: 48 m — the perimeter, 2 × (15 + 9), because edging and covering are different jobs

questions.question: A 20 litre urn pouring 250 ml cups serves 120 guests:
options: No — 20 000 ÷ 250 = 80 cups falls short of 120; two urns give 160, with 40 spare
No — an urn pours only 20 cups

questions.question: 180 km at an average 90 km/h is:
For an 09:30 arrival with 2 hours of driving plus half an hour of stops, departure is:
options: 07:00 — subtract the driving to 07:30, then the stops

questions.question: The gravel road measures 12 cm on a 1 : 50 000 map. Its real length:
options: 6 km — 600 000 cm down the unit ladder

questions.question: The bakkie uses 8 litres per 100 km at R23,50 per litre. The 180 km trip costs:
A 30% chance of rain, written as a fraction and a decimal:
Rain fell on this weekend in 4 of the last 20 years. The experimental probability is:
What a 30% rain chance does NOT mean:
options: Rain is less likely than dry weather
On days like this, rain has arrived about 3 times in 10
That it will rain for 30% of the day or over 30% of the district

questions.question: A full-marks answer on hiring the R850 gazebo:
options: Either choice, stated with its reason — weighing the gazebo's cost against the cost of 120 soaked guests
